analysis: Examined test-only changes. CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift (head 10-12, 21) changes its documentation: the suite now runs in the provider CI lane (scripts/run-provider-tests.sh) and is no longer described as skipped. The suite adds tests 3c/3d (head 456-491). Test 3c checks that a coordinator-side 1012 close reconnects within 1.5 s. Test 3d checks that a session open past stableSessionDuration resets the backoff. The suite also adds helpers: makeClient takes a reconnectPolicy (head 652-676), reregistrationTime calls mock.dropActiveWebSocket(closeCode:reason:) (head 681-693), and withGrownReconnectBackoff is new (head 699-727). The added CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift is visible only through its patch excerpt; the unit carries file metadata with no citable lines. Its tests cover: a backoff reset after sessions of 60 s or more, a 0-1 s wait without growth for close code 1012, and the unchanged ExponentialBackoff ranges otherwise. No production source is in this batch, so no regression can be cited here. Integration must examine the production CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and the runLoop change; their source is not supplied. Availability-relevant questions (TB-002, ADV-003, A-018): 1) Is the fast-reconnect path for close code 1012 bounded against an adversarial or on-path peer that sends repeated 1012 frames? TLS should limit who can close the socket, but sustained tight reconnect loops or fleet-wide thundering-herd load on the coordinator should be checked. Does 1012 keep jitter (0-1 s)? Does it avoid resetting the growth counter in a way that permits an unbounded fast loop? 2) Does the stable-session reset rely on monotonic clock time? 3) Reconnect must preserve T-053 endpoint-resumption semantics: a fresh socket nonce, a re-registration and no carried-over grants. These tests only show that re-registration occurs. The test at head 469-470 also implies 1012 reconnects skip the grown backoff. The MockCoordinator close-code support is test infrastructure only.
